text:
Olivia: Heads up — noticing allocator spike + controller lag causing bursty tenant overruns this morning. thinking about adding a rate-cap at the controller level to damp oscillation. anyone seen this pattern before?
Sam: yep saw similar last quarter. controller applies desired_scale then operator reconciles slower -> double-provision for a window. rate-cap helped but needed per-tenant nuance.
Maria: can you paste a short trace? is this the prewarm+burst double-booking case or pure scale-up loop?
Olivia: trace: 10m of sustained intent, controller pushed +3 replicas, operator took 3m to create nodes, meanwhile requests kept queuing so controller pushed another +2. end result: temporary 5x headroom.
Jun: thinking aloud: two failure modes — (1) controller overshoot due to stale metrics, (2) operator slow create. rate-cap helps (1) but (2) needs backpressure to callers or token-banking.
Priya: we already have tenant warmup credits. Problem is credits get consumed fast when controller spikes. if we put a controller-side rate limit, we need a safe fallback: either reject or throttle. rejection causes upstream errors.
Sam: option sketch: controller enforces a 2-step admission: quick soft-increase (fast path) up to 'burst_headroom' then slow reconciliation to final target. soft-increase bounded by a per-tenant token bucket that refills slowly.
Maria: +1 but must avoid starvation for low-volume tenants. token bucket parameters should be a function of tenant SLO tier + recent usage.
Olivia: alternative: integral correction in controller that decays the scale command when operator lag is detected. e.g. if last_applied_age > T then cap new desired_delta = max(0, desired_delta - k*age).
Jun: that buys stability but we still need fairness across tenants during cluster-wide provisioning delays. what if one tenant consumes all burst tokens and others degrade?
Priya: we could introduce a soft global headroom pool and per-tenant nominal buckets. when global pool exhausted, enforce proportional fairness: scale downs or deny fast-paths based on weights.
Sam: implementation notes: 1) add controller metric "operator_apply_lag_seconds" 2) add admission decision component that looks at operator_lag + per-tenant-balance + global-pool 3) expose decisions in telemetry.
Olivia: sample pseudocode: ```
admit_fast_path(tenant, delta):
  if operator_lag > L: return false
  if tenant.tokens >= delta: tenant.tokens -= delta; return true
  if global_pool >= delta: global_pool -= delta; mark_replenish(); return true
  return false
```
Jun: love the pseudocode — add hysteresis so we don't flip fast-path on/off every 30s. maybe require sustained operator_lag < L for 2 windows before reopening.
Maria: also add a safetynet route: if request latency climbs above X and we have spare capacity in dedicated pools, allow emergency borrow across pools (with cost accounting) rather than immediate rejection.
Priya: ops question: how do we surface when controller is throttling tenants? logs alone won't help. need per-tenant admission traces + alert when throttle rate > 1% of requests.
deploy-bot: deployment report: autoscaler v0.42 rolled 02/06 03:12 UTC to canary (3 nodes). health: ok.
Sam: roll plan: prototype controller admission locally, add metrics + canary with small tenant set, observe headroom/overshoot. If stable, roll to 10% clusters.
Olivia: agreed. I'll draft a short RFC with operator_lag metric, token-bucket defaults, global pool policy, and telemetry requirements. assigning myself to initial prototype.
Maria: happy to review the RFC and help wire telemetry dashboards.
Jun: I'll look into operator-side faster apply optimizations in parallel — we should tackle both sides.
Priya: I'll coordinate on alert thresholds and playbook for emergency-borrow.
Olivia: thanks all — will post RFC link when ready. :raised_hands:
